rationale: TestEveryActionInputSpecHasARegistryEntry had been failing at committed HEAD since the bugfix-136 probe actions landed, and it was failing in the most misleading way a test can: `go test -run TestEveryActionInputSpecHasARegistryEntry` PASSES on its own name while `go test ./platform/orchestration/actions/` FAILS, so the obvious way to check whether it is your fault reports that it is not. The cause is that the ActionInputSpec registry is a PROCESS-GLOBAL map with a Register function and no removal path, so a spec registered by any test in the package to probe spec behaviour is visible to this test - but only when the whole package runs, and only when the registering file sorts earlier (create_work_item_config_contract_test.go does). The two probe specs are named test_only_bug136_create_work_item_without_configkeys and its _control sibling; they are fixtures, not actions, and they deliberately have no GlobalActionRegistry entry because they do not exist. THE FIX IS AT THE ASSUMPTION, NOT AT THE OTHER LANE'S FILE: this test assumed every registered spec names a real action, and that has not been true since a test needed to register one. Skipping names prefixed test_only_ states the exemption where the assumption lives, and leaves the bugfix-136 lane's probe untouched. I considered and REJECTED adding an UnregisterActionInputSpec helper so the probe could clean up after itself, which is the fix-at-source version: it would add a new EXPORTED SYMBOL to platform/orchestration/datahelpers, a package three other packages import, which under PROCESS_architecture_review's trigger test is architecture-scope - a disproportionate route for a test-only concern, and it would also hand every future caller a way to mutate the live registry at runtime, which is a strictly worse capability to own than a prefix convention. THE RISK THIS CHANGE CARRIES IS THAT IT NARROWS A DETECTOR, and this estate has a filed pattern for narrowing one until it is inert, so the non-vacuity was measured rather than argued: with the skip in place I registered a genuine non-fixture spec with no registry entry (mutation_probe_not_a_real_action) and the test FAILED on it, naming it, with the full guidance message intact. The detector still catches exactly what it exists to catch.

plan.summary: Make the registry-parity test skip ActionInputSpec names prefixed test_only_, so a test fixture registered into the process-global spec registry stops failing the whole package while passing under -run. Fixes the wrong assumption (every registered spec is an action) rather than the other lane's probe, and rejects the fix-at-source alternative because an Unregister helper would be a new exported symbol on a package three others import. Non-vacuity measured: a genuine unregistered spec still fails the test.

edits.rationale: One guard clause plus the strings import. The comment states the mechanism (process-global registry, no removal path, ordering-dependent visibility), records the -run-passes/package-fails asymmetry that makes this expensive to diagnose, and names the rejected alternative with the reason - so the next author who wonders why this is not fixed at source does not have to re-derive the architecture-scope argument. It also tells fixture authors to keep using the prefix, which is what keeps the convention working.

plan.risks: THE REAL RISK IS DETECTOR NARROWING, and it is the reason this is submitted rather than treated as trivial housekeeping. A skip rule can quietly make a check inert, and this estate has that pattern on file. Two things bound it. First, measured non-vacuity: with the skip in place, registering a genuine non-fixture spec that has no GlobalActionRegistry entry (mutation_probe_not_a_real_action) still FAILS the test and names the offender, with the full 'add an entry to registry.go, or add it to dormantActions' guidance intact - so the detector catches exactly what it exists to catch. Second, the exemption is narrow and self-announcing: it is keyed to a literal prefix that no live action carries and that reads as deliberately non-production at every call site. RESIDUAL EXPOSURE, stated rather than argued away: a real action named with a test_only_ prefix would now be skipped silently. That is a naming collision nobody has an incentive to create, it would be visible in review, and the alternative (no exemption at all) leaves the package red for everyone, which is strictly worse - a permanently failing test is not a detector, because nobody reads its output. WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX: the underlying design, which is a process-global mutable registry with a Register and no Unregister. Any test that needs a fixture spec must keep using the prefix, and the comment says so. Converging that properly is the architecture-scope change deliberately not bundled here. SCOPE: one test file, no non-test code, no behaviour change to any action, no schema, no migration, no config vocabulary, no wire shape, no exported symbol added or changed. Inert in production by construction - a _test.go file is not compiled into the chassis binary, so there is nothing to roll and nothing to pod-grep. ROLLBACK is deleting nine lines. BLAST RADIUS is the CI/test signal only, and it moves it from permanently-red to green-with-a-live-detector.
grounded_in: The failure at committed HEAD, reproduced against a clean `git archive HEAD` tree rather than the shared working tree (which carries other sessions' WIP in this same package): `go test ./platform/orchestration/actions/` reports `--- FAIL: TestEveryActionInputSpecHasARegistryEntry`, while `go test ./platform/orchestration/actions/ -run TestEveryActionInputSpecHasARegistryEntry` reports `ok`. The two results are both real and the second is the misleading one.

The registering fixture, platform/orchestration/actions/create_work_item_config_contract_test.go:153-172, which registers two specs into the global registry and has no cleanup because none is available: 'const probe = "test_only_bug136_create_work_item_without_configkeys"; stripped := CreateWorkItemInputSpec; stripped.ConfigKeys = nil; datahelpers.RegisterActionInputSpec(probe, stripped)' and, for its control arm, 'datahelpers.RegisterActionInputSpec(probe+"_control", off)'.

The test's own assumption, registry_parity_test.go: it iterates 'datahelpers.ListActionInputSpecNames()' and requires every name to be present in GlobalActionRegistry or in dormantActions. A fixture is in neither, and cannot honestly be added to dormantActions - that map means 'a real action deliberately unreachable', which a probe spec is not.

The absence of a removal path, confirmed by grep over platform/orchestration/datahelpers/action_inputs.go: 'func RegisterActionInputSpec' (:712) and 'func ListActionInputSpecNames' (:726) exist; there is no UnregisterActionInputSpec, no Reset, and no test hook. So the fixture cannot clean up after itself today.

The architecture-scope reason the fix-at-source alternative was rejected, PROCESS_architecture_review.md's trigger test as amended and owner-confirmed on 2026-08-10: a change needs an RFC when 'it adds, changes or removes an exported symbol other packages depend on'. An Unregister helper on datahelpers is exactly that.

Measured non-vacuity, run before submission: with the skip in place, adding 'datahelpers.RegisterActionInputSpec("mutation_probe_not_a_real_action", datahelpers.ActionInputSpec{CheckConfig: true})' to the test makes it FAIL with 'action "mutation_probe_not_a_real_action" registers an ActionInputSpec but has no GlobalActionRegistry entry', guidance message intact. Reverted after the check.

Post-change state at a clean `git archive HEAD` tree: platform/orchestration, platform/orchestration/actions, platform/orchestration/datahelpers and platform/validation all report 'ok'. The actions package was red before this change.
